brief:
Nearly 60 percent of voting faculty members at the University of Michigan have backed a resolution supporting a dozen former students and staff who face charges, the Middle East Eye reported. The resolution affirmed solidarity with the dozen individuals targeted in connection with pro-Palestine activism on campus.

University administrators have pursued charges against activists following demonstrations related to the Gaza conflict. The faculty vote reflects tension between university leadership and faculty over how the institution has responded to campus protest.
